LESSON: RESPIRATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.5: Respiration
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Respiration, part of Life Science in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is aerobic and anaerobic respiration important in a society’s economy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the meaning of respiration in living things,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Respiration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe aerobic and anaerobic respiration in living things,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Respiration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Respiration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Respiration together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses with peers the factors affecting energy requirements in human

beings.

• Learning to learn: as the learner uses print media with appropriate colour contrast and fonts or braille learning resources

to search for information on aerobic and anaerobic respiration in living organisms.

Values:
● Integrity: as the learner observes ethical behaviours when working on a project of value addition of food products that

utilises the concept of aerobic respiration.

• Peace: as the learner works harmoniously with peers in carrying out a project that utilises the concept of anaerobic

respiration such as making of yoghurt, porridge, biogas.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Financial literacy: as the learner undertakes a project that utilises the concept

of anaerobic respiration in value addition of food products such as milk and flour

• Socio Economic and environmental issues - Environmental conservation: as the learner develops the skill of making

biogas as an alternative source of fuel (energy).
